provider: Common Crawl (the petabyte corpus — read side only)

free_tier.stated: Not a hosting service: ~300 billion web pages across ~100+ monthly crawls, multi-petabyte, free to READ and free to re-host yourself. There is NO path to host your own data with Common Crawl — confirmed, it publishes its own crawls only.

egress.terms: Free and anonymous over HTTPS: 'The data is accessible via the https://data.commoncrawl.org/[...] URL scheme. There is no need to create an AWS account in order to access the data using this method.' S3 access (s3://commoncrawl) requires an authenticated AWS account. New: selected crawls are mirrored into a Hugging Face Storage Bucket with CDN pre-warming.

tooling: wget/curl against data.commoncrawl.org, aws-cli against s3://commoncrawl (auth), the pycrawl / cc-index-table Athena tooling, and now `hf buckets cp hf://buckets/commoncrawl/commoncrawl/...`.
chaining: Read-side: any amount of free inbound bandwidth for corpus you would otherwise have to build. The useful pattern for a user is the reverse of storage — Common Crawl is the SOURCE that makes a 200 GB Kaggle/generic pipeline interesting without owning a petabyte.
limits_note: WARC files are ~1 GB each, ~300k of them; us-east-1 locality strongly recommended ('It's mandatory to access the data from the region where it is located'); the public S3 listing at commoncrawl.s3.amazonaws.com returns 403 to unauthenticated callers (probed) — use HTTPS or HF instead.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Extremely stable (running since 2008, sponsored by AWS), immutable crawl archives, no access throttling observed on the HTTPS path.

evidence.proved: 'There is no need to create an AWS account in order to access the data using this method'; 'access to data from the Amazon cloud using the S3 API is only allowed for authenticated users'
probe: GET -> 200, 201,605 bytes, gzip (anonymous listing manifest)
